([[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]]) | college = * [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure]] (2017–2018) * [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]] (2019–2021) * [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] (2021–2022) | draftyear = 2022 | career_start = 2023 | career_end = | years1 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team1 = [[Birmingham Squadron]] | years2 = {{nbay|2023|end}} | team2 = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | years3 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team3 = →Birmingham Squadron | years5 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team5 = [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] | years6 = 2025 | team6 = [[Vancouver Bandits]] | years7 = 2025–2026 | team7 = [[New Zealand Breakers]] | highlights = * [[NBL Ignite Cup]] winner ([[2025–26 NBL Ignite Cup|2026]]) * First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2022) * Big 12 Newcomer of the Year (2022) }} '''Izaiah Antoine Brockington''' (born July 12, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure Bonnies]], [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State Nittany Lions]], and [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. ==High school career== Brockington played basketball for [[Archbishop Ryan High School]] in [[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]]. He entered the starting lineup as a sophomore.{{cite web |last1=Gallen |first1=Daniel |title=After putting Archbishop Ryan 'on the map' with historic season, Izaiah Brockington and his fellow seniors move on |url=https://www.pennlive.com/highschoolsports/article/after-putting-archbishop-ryan-on-the-map-with-historic-season-izaiah-brockington-and-his-fellow-seniors-move-on/ |website=[[The Patriot-News]] |access-date=November 29, 2021 |date=March 22, 2017}} In his senior season, Brockington averaged 18.6 points per game and led his team to its first Class 6A semifinals appearance. He finished his high school career with 1,242 career points, becoming the third 1,000-point scorer in program history.{{cite web |last1=Gallen |first1=Daniel |title=Transfer Izaiah Brockington, a Philly native, announces commitment to Penn State |url=https://www.pennlive.com/sports/2018/04/transfer_izaiah_brockington_a.html |website=[[The Patriot-News]] |access-date=November 29, 2021 |date=April 28, 2018}} Brockington originally committed to playing college basketball for [[NJIT Highlanders men's basketball|NJIT]] in August 2016, before announcing he would do a prep year at [[Woodstock Academy]] in [[Woodstock, Connecticut]]. In August 2017, he instead signed with [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure]].{{cite web |last1=Carter |first1=Aaron |title=Archbishop Ryan grad Izaiah Brockington to play hoops at St. Bonaventure |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/high_school/pennsylvania/st-bonaventure-basketball-izaiah-brockington-archbishop-ryan-point-guard-20170808.html |website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |access-date=November 29, 2021 |date=August 8, 2017}} ==College career== As a freshman at St. Bonaventure, Brockington averaged 4.3 points and 1.2 rebounds per game. He transferred to [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]] for his sophomore season.{{cite web |last1=Hunt |first1=Donald |title=Sports Notes: Ex-Archbishop Ryan star Izaiah Brockington transfers to Penn State |url=https://www.phillytrib.com/sports/basketball/sports-notes-ex-archbishop-ryan-star-izaiah-brockington-transfers-to-penn-state/article_79b37130-95c6-5c10-bc44-99e95c67ed12.html |website=[[The Philadelphia Tribune]] |access-date=November 29, 2021 |date=May 18, 2018}} Brockington sat out for one season due to NCAA transfer rules. He assumed a [[sixth man]] role as a sophomore, averaging 8.1 points and 2.7 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Stepien |first1=Garrett |title=Penn State guard Izaiah Brockington re-enters NCAA transfer portal |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Izaiah-Brockington-transfer-portal-Penn-State-Nittany-Lions-basketball-NCAA-164514698/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=November 29, 2021 |date=April 22, 2021}} In his junior year, Brockington became a regular starter, and averaged 12.6 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game. He scored a season-high 24 points against [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] and had 18 double-figure scoring performances. For his senior season, Brockington transferred to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].{{cite web |title=Iowa State Cyclones add versatile Izaiah Brockington from Penn State Nittany Lions |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31399585/iowa-state-cyclones-add-versatile-izaiah-brockington-penn-state-nittany-lions |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=November 29, 2021}} He entered the [[2021 NBA draft]] before withdrawing his name.{{cite web |last1=Swain |first1=Michael |title=Izaiah Brockington reportedly withdraws from 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa-state/Article/Iowa-State-basketball-news-Izaiah-Brockington-reportedly-withdraws-from-2021-NBA-Draft-167292557/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=November 29, 2021 |date=July 1, 2021}} On November 24, 2021, Brockington scored 30 points in an 82–70 win against [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]].{{cite web |title=Brockington scores 30, Iowa State beats No. 25 Xavier 82-70 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401372039 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=November 29, 2021 |date=November 24, 2021}} He scored a career-high 35 points in an 84–81 win against [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] on February 23, 2022.{{cite news |title=Brockington brings Iowa State back, tops West Virginia 84-81 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401368426 |access-date=February 24, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 23, 2022}} For the season, Brockington averaged 16.9 points, 6.8 rebounds, and 1.6 assists per game. He was named to the First Team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] as well as Big 12 Newcomer of the Year.{{cite news |last1=Peterson |first1=Randy |title=It's unanimous: Iowa State's Izaiah Brockington a first-team pick, Big 12 newcomer of the year |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2022/03/08/iowa-state-cyclones-basketball-izaiah-brockington-ap-all-big-12-conference-first-team/9413608002/ |access-date=March 10, 2022 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=March 8, 2022}} On March 28, 2022, Brockington announced he would forego his additional year of eligibility and declare for the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |date=2022-03-28 |title=ISU's Brockington and Conditt IV to pursue pro careers |url=https://www.kjan.com/index.php/2022/03/isus-brockington-and-conditt-iv-to-pursue-pro-careers/ |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=KJAN |language=en-US}} ==Professional career== ===Birmingham Squadron / New Orleans Pelicans (2023–2025)=== Brockington suffered an [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|ACL injury]] during a pre-draft workout.{{cite news |title=Pelicans sign Izaiah Brockington {{!}} New Orleans Pelicans |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-izaiah-brockington-roster-update |access-date=28 July 2025 |work=www.nba.com |date=13 September 2022 |language=en}} He subsequently went undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. On September 13, 2022, Brockington signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. He was later waived on September 24.{{cite news |title=Pelicans sign John Butler and Zylan Cheatham {{!}} New Orleans Pelicans |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-john-butler-zylan-cheatham-waive-izaiah-brockington-roster |access-date=28 July 2025 |work=www.nba.com |date=24 September 2022 |language=en}} On March 14, 2023, Brockington was acquired by the [[Birmingham Squadron]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=Birmingham Announces Addition of Izaiah Brockington|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-announced-addition-of-izaiah-brockington|website=NBA.com|date=March 14, 2023|access-date=March 14, 2023}} He appeared in two games to finish the [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–23 season]].{{cite web |title=Izaiah Brockington Player Profile, New Orleans Pelicans - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Izaiah-Brockington/Summary/121603 |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=28 July 2025 |language=en}} Brockington played for the New Orleans Pelicans during the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]. On October 16, 2023, he signed with the Pelicans,{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans sign Izaiah Brockington|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-sign-izaiah-brockington-waive-landers-nolley-ii|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2023|access-date=October 17, 2023}} but was waived six days later.{{cite news |title=New Orleans Pelicans announce roster moves {{!}} New Orleans Pelicans |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/matt-ryan-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-moves-announced-102223 |access-date=28 July 2025 |work=www.nba.com |date=22 October 2023 |language=en}} He subsequently re-joined the Birmingham Squadron for the [[2023–24 NBA G League season]].{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron Finalize Training Camp Roster|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-squadron-finalize-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=November 3, 2023}} On March 3, 2024, Brockington signed a 10-day contract with the Pelicans.{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign guard Izaiah Brockington to 10-day contract|url=https://crescentcitysports.com/pelicans-sign-guard-izaiah-brockington-to-10-day-contract/|website=CrescentCitySports.com|date=March 3, 2024|access-date=March 3, 2024}} On March 5, he made his NBA debut, playing three minutes against the [[Toronto Raptors]]. It marked his only NBA game.{{cite web |title=Izaiah Brockington 2023-24 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/brockiz01/gamelog/2024/ |website=basketball-reference.com |access-date=28 July 2025}} He was assigned twice to Birmingham during his ten days with the Pelicans. On March 14, he returned to Birmingham permanently.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Birmingham Squadron Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Birmingham-Squadron/59/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 14, 2024}} Brockington played for the New Orleans Pelicans during the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]. He signed with the Pelicans once again on September 24, 2024,{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign three players|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/izaiah-brockington-keion-brooks-jr-galen-robinson-jr-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-additions-september-24-2024|website=NBA.com|date=September 24, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}} but was waived on October 1.{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Adonis Arms|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/adonis-arms-guard-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-2024-training-camp|website=NBA.com|date=October 1, 2024|access-date=October 1, 2024}} He subsequently re-joined the Squadron for the [[2024–25 NBA G League season]].{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-squadron-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} ===San Diego Clippers (2025)=== On March 4, 2025, Brockington was traded to the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]]. ===Vancouver Bandits (2025)=== On April 4, 2025, Brockington signed with the [[Vancouver Bandits]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=Vancouver Bandits Sign NBA Experienced Guard, Big 12 All-Star Izaiah Brockington|url=https://www.thebandits.ca/vancouver-bandits-sign-nba-experienced-guard-big-12-all-star-izaiah-brockington|website=thebandits.ca|date=April 4, 2025|access-date=June 8, 2024}} Brockington joined the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]]. ===New Zealand Breakers (2025–2026)=== On July 28, 2025, Brockington signed with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the [[2025–26 NBL season|2025–26 season]].{{cite news |title=Breakers sign former G League star |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/report-breakers-sign-former-g-league-star |access-date=28 July 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=28 July 2025 |language=en}} The Breakers finished outside the finals spots in seventh at the end of the regular season but won the inaugural [[2025–26 NBL Ignite Cup|NBL Ignite Cup]] Final,{{cite news |title=MVP call backfires with NBL title contender stunned as non-finalist pulls upset in $400k final |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/mvp-call-backfires-with-nbl-title-contender-stunned-as-nonfinalist-pulls-upset-in-400k-final/news-story/87d6c19cb9ae35133a326f099e099f16 |access-date=22 February 2026 |work=Fox Sports |date=22 February 2026 |language=en}} defeating the [[Adelaide 36ers]] 111–107 behind Brockington's 21 points.{{cite news |title=Mennenga seals Breakers' dramatic Ignite triumph {{!}} Basketball.com.au |url=https://www.basketball.com.au/news/parker-jackson-cartwright-ignite-cup-dagger-breakers-36ers-feb-22-2026 |access-date=22 February 2026
